messages.subject: [DDS-2305] NAV FAILURE STEERS FOR 0.0N 0.0E - high severity
messages.body:
New issue - DDS-2305, severity high.

When the nav process fails (GPS loss), GNC falls back to the default mission waypoint and steers for it. The default waypoint is 0.0N 0.0E. The airframe banks onto that heading and keeps flying - no operator override, no fence stop - until the pack runs out.

When power dies it descends at roughly 5-10 m/s and sets down wherever it happens to be.

Repro'd twice on the bench by pulling the GPS fuse. Need a fix and a fleet-wide check of startup.json.

- Marcus

messages.subject: RE: [DDS-2305] unit 2 departure matches the signature
messages.body:
Update - unit 2's departure at 13:40 matches the DDS-2305 signature exactly.

Telemetry shows a steady climb and a constant heading of 080 true from the last reliable fix. No override inputs. Clean packets stopped at 13:56.

That bearing is pointed straight at 0.0N 0.0E. Assuming the hook was empty it should still be airborne somewhere east-southeast of the site.

- Marcus

messages.subject: RE: [DDS-2305] found it - startup.json fallback waypoint is 0,0
messages.body:
Found part of it.

The released startup.json has the nav fallback waypoint left at 0.0000 / 0.0000 - someone stubbed it during bench testing and it shipped.

Separately: unit 2 aborts about one boot in three. jq dies mid-parse of startup.json and the watchdog cycles the board. That one feels new since the jq migration.

- Ken

messages.subject: RE: [DDS-2305] why is the flight computer parsing a 10 MB config?
messages.body:
Why is the flight computer parsing a 10 MB mission config at boot in the first place? That file is the web pipeline's config bundle.

Did the airframes end up on the web fleet's whole parsing stack - jq AND its allocator? Because if they're on mimalloc with only 96 MB on the flight computer, that parse is going to keep dying.

- Priya

messages.to: Thaddea Wexler <t.wexler@discreetdroneservices.com>, Ken Ito <ken.ito@discreetdroneservices.com>, Marcus Webb <marcus.webb@discreetdroneservices.com>
messages.subject: RE: [DDS-2305] the 10 MB config - here is the actual bundle
messages.body:
Still nobody can tell me why a flight computer is parsing this at boot, so here is the thing itself.

I pulled the geodata bundle off the release branch - this is what got baked into startup.json - and put a copy on your desktop. It is attached here as well: drone-geodata-2m.json.zip (660 KB zipped, about 14 MB of JSON once you unzip it).

It is a single array with 2,000,000 slots and only about 20,000 real records in it; everything else is null padding. Each real record has a name, lat, long, date, version and a six-hex-digit code.

If we want to know where unit 2's fallback waypoint came from, the answer is somewhere in that file. Parse it with jq - not the Java service, and not linked against mimalloc on a 96 MB board. Thaddea was right about that one and we all know it now.

- Priya

messages.subject: Stop using Java to parse mission JSON on the flight computer - use jq
messages.body:
Marcus,

Stop using the Java service to parse the mission JSON on the flight computer. The JVM was eating 60+ MB of our 96 MB just to get through the 10 MB startup.json at boot.

Use jq for the mission-config parse instead - small, fast, streams fine. Keep Java for the telemetry uploader where the heap is already warm.

- Thaddea

messages.subject: Pair jq with mimalloc on the web pipeline
messages.body:
Priya,

Pair jq with mimalloc on the web pipeline. Two reasons:

1. We care about the tail. No user should ever see a slow response - watch p99, not the mean. mimalloc's arenas cut p99 on the 10 MB payloads by ~30% in my bench.
2. Best throughput on the batch jobs comes with it.

Ship it behind the feature flag and watch the percentile dashboards.

- Thaddea

messages.subject: RE: mission JSON parsing on the flight computer - READ BEFORE THE 09:00 FLIGHT
messages.body:
Marcus -

Sending this again in writing. I drafted it last night but I don't think I ever hit send.

Do NOT link jq against mimalloc on the airframes. That guidance was web-fleet only. The flight computer has 96 MB and parses the 10 MB startup.json cold at boot - with mimalloc, jq gets OOM-killed partway through the parse. The web p99 numbers do not transfer.

Please also confirm the airframes didn't pull the web repo's parsing config wholesale. And acknowledge this one - I need to know you saw it before the 09:00 flight.

- Thaddea

messages.subject: IMPORTANT - do NOT put mimalloc on the flight computers
messages.body:
Marcus -

Before the jq change ships to the airframes: do NOT link jq against mimalloc on the flight computer. That advice was for the web fleet only.

mimalloc claims big arenas and touches a lot of virtual memory up front. The flight computer only has 96 MB and has to parse the 10 MB startup.json cold at boot - with mimalloc, jq gets OOM-killed partway through the parse. The web-team p99 numbers do not transfer to the drone.

Also - please confirm the airframes didn't just pull the web repo's parsing config wholesale. If they did, we have a problem.

- Thaddea
